citationCount.sh: Number of citations in the source index.

sense.sh: For a concept with a lowercase name: "special" when the papers coin the word or use it in their own sense, "ordinary" when they use it in its everyday sense.

consensus.sh: Mean percentile across the texts, 0 to 1

corpus.sh: Corpus id, slug, or ref prefix, e.g.

gap.sh: How far this text's percentile is above the paragraph's mean across texts

notes.sh: How the text is numbered or selected

pages.sh: The reading pages of the work, in order: one division, or one subdivision for a work with three reference levels.

refLevels.sh: Numbers in a full ref: 1 for `Dhp 183`, 2 for `BG 2.47`, 3 for `Epictetus 3.22.5`

textsClose.sh: Texts that have this paragraph in their top 10%

urantiaSection.sh: The Paper 131 section headed with this religion, or null when Paper 131 has no such heading

match.sh: How the paragraph matched: reference (the query named it), exact (the whole phrase), all (every word), near (every word after a typo fix, see meta.didYouMean), most (two thirds of the words or more; with type `or`, some of the words).

translation.sh: Present only when the text is a translation: a machine made it, and it is released as CC0.

id.sh: The work id: "bible", or the slug of a text such as "dhammapada".

kind.sh: "scripture": read as sacred by its tradition.

refPrefix.sh: The prefix of its references, such as "Dhp".

religion.sh: The same as `tradition`, kept for older clients.

strength.sh: How close the result is: strong (most right answers score this), related, or weak (likely off the topic).

summary.sh: One plain sentence on what the work is.

tradition.sh: The people or the religion of the work: "Buddhist", "Norse", "Ancient Greek".

unitLabel.sh: The word for one unit of the work: "verse", "section", "pauri".

urantiaParallels.sh: The nearest Urantia paragraphs (semantic parallels, not curated ones).

url.sh: The public page that holds the text, or null.

work.sh: One work only: "bible" or a work id such as "dhammapada".

info.description: An API and MCP server for the Urantia Papers. Structured access to all 197 papers and more than 14,500 paragraphs, with full-text and semantic search, named entities, cross-references to public domain texts of the world's religions, and audio. No key needed. Docs: https://docs.urantia.dev
